title: Difference Quotient of a Quadratic
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: For f(x)=x^2, compute and simplify the difference quotient (f(x+h)-f(x))/h, assuming h != 0.

steps.title: Form the Two Function Values
steps.explanation: Replace every x in the rule by x+h to get the incremented value.
steps.why: The difference quotient measures the change caused by the increment h.

steps.title: Expand and Subtract
steps.explanation: Expanding gives x^2+2xh+h^2, and the x^2 terms cancel in the numerator.
steps.why: Cancellation of f(x) leaves only terms containing the increment h.

steps.title: Divide by h
steps.explanation: Factor h from the numerator and cancel it against the denominator (valid since h != 0).
steps.why: Every surviving numerator term contains h, so the quotient simplifies completely.
